highlights:
USMNT’
[...]
Brazil: Yeah, count me all in on Brazil.
[...]
Vinicius Junior is one of my favorite players and there’s a ton of potential for him to just BALL OUT this summer.
[...]
Brazil is winning Group C. I’m sorry Morocco, but this is Brazil’s time to shine.
[...]
The Selecao will beat the Group F runner-up in the round of 32. The round-of-16 matchup is against either the Group E runner-up or Group I runner-up.
[...]
If England and Mexico win their groups, Brazil likely faces one of them in the quarterfinals.
[...]
Brazil is even-money to reach the quarterfinal and +220 to reach the semifinal. Yep, I’m in.
[...]
Furthermore, give me Vinicius to win the Golden Boot at +2500. There’s four really good scoring opportunities on the run-in to the quarterfinal and maybe a fifth if Brazil overpowers Morocco.
[...]
Sure, Igor Thiago and Matheus Cunha and Raphinha exist and goals will come from them as well, but Vini is the star and he’s the star I’m willing to throw a good chunk of money behind this summer.
[...]
Morocco: Morocco is finishing second in Group C. There’s no debate on this one. Morocco can put up six points on Scotland and Haiti. I think Brazil dominates on goal differential, so even if Brazil and Morocco are level on seven points, the Selecao clear the field.

Picks: Brazil To Reach Quarterfinals (+100; bet365); Morocco To Finish Second In Group C (+100; DK) Scotland Under 4.5 Tournament Goals (-120; DK); Haiti To Advance From Group Stage (+800; DK)
[...]
Both teams should take six points from games against Saudi Arabia and Cape Verde. We can probably just fast forward to June 26, when the clash between the two sides happens at the Estadio Akron.
[...]
Saudi Arabia and Cape Verde: I’m going to root for a fun story in third place, so I’ll take Cape Verde to beat Saudi Arabia on Matchday 3 and reach the round of 32.
[...]
Cape Verde is +275 to be eliminated in the round of 32, which is realistically its ceiling. Saudi Arabia is -150 to be eliminated in the group stage. The odds suck there, but I don’t think the Saudis are long for the tournament.
[...]
Plus Saudi Arabia already had its cool World Cup moment with the win over Argentina four years ago. Let’s let Cape Verde be celebrated instead this time around.
